q: Alkene molecules are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon _____ bond.
e: Alkene molecules are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond. Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, so alkenes, alkynes and aromatics sit in that group. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds.

q: The ethylenic bond is the _____ group of an alkene, and largely dictates their reactions.
e: The ethylenic bond is the functional group of an alkene, and largely dictates their reactions. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: Alkenes form a homologous series with the general formula _____.
e: Alkenes form a homologous series with the general formula C_nH2n. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once.

q: The first member of the alkene series is known as _____.
e: The first member of the alkene series is known as ethene. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.

q: In the IUPAC system for naming alkenes, the chain is numbered starting at the end nearest to the _____.
e: In the IUPAC system for naming alkenes, the chain is numbered starting at the end nearest to the double bond. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.

q: In alkenes, isomers that have the same carbon skeleton and the same functional groups but differ in the location of the functional groups are called _____ isomers.
e: In alkenes, isomers that have the same carbon skeleton and the same functional groups but differ in the location of the functional groups are called positional isomers. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule. Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ.

q: Two methods may be used for the dehydration of alcohols, one of which is heating with concentrated sulphuric acid at _____.
e: Two methods may be used for the dehydration of alcohols, one of which is heating with concentrated sulphuric acid at 160 degreesC. Concentrated sulphuric acid is viscous, dehydrating and oxidising as well as strongly acidic. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. Concentrated sulphuric acid is a strong acid, a dehydrating agent and an oxidising agent.

q: Ethene can be prepared from ethanol by passing the vapours over heated alumina ($Al_2O_3$) at _____.
e: Ethene can be prepared from ethanol by passing the vapours over heated alumina (Al_2O_3) at 350 degreesC. Ethene can be prepared from ethanol by passing.

q: Dehydrohalogenation is used when a halogen atom and a hydrogen atom on an adjacent carbon are simultaneously removed as _____.
e: Dehydrohalogenation is used when a halogen atom and a hydrogen atom on an adjacent carbon are simultaneously removed as hydrogen halide. Atom and a hydrogen atom on an adjacent.

q: At room temperature, alkenes containing two to four carbon atoms are _____.
e: At room temperature, alkenes containing two to four carbon atoms are gases. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n. Gases is the word this version is asking about.

q: Alkenes burn in the air with a luminous, _____ flame.
e: Alkenes burn in the air with a luminous, smoky flame. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.

q: The unsaturated nature of alkenes is shown in their _____ reactions.
e: The unsaturated nature of alkenes is shown in their addition reactions. Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, so alkenes, alkynes and aromatics sit in that group. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n. In an addition reaction atoms add across a double or triple bond and unsaturation falls.

q: The addition of $Br_2$ to alkenes is used as a simple qualitative test for _____.
e: The addition of Br_2 to alkenes is used as a simple qualitative test for unsaturation. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n. Unsaturation is the word this version is asking about.

q: When an alkene is added to bromine water, the reddish-brown solution becomes _____ as the $Br_2$ reacts.
e: When an alkene is added to bromine water, the reddish-brown solution becomes colourless as the Br_2 reacts. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.

q: Markownikoff's rule states that when an unsymmetrical addendum adds on to an unsymmetrical alkene, the negative part of the addendum adds on to the carbon with the _____ number of hydrogen atoms.
e: Markownikoff's rule states that when an unsymmetrical addendum adds on to an unsymmetrical alkene, the negative part of the addendum adds on to the carbon with the least number of hydrogen atoms. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.

q: The complete process of preparing the ozonide followed by decomposing it is called _____.
e: The complete process of preparing the ozonide followed by decomposing it is called ozonolysis. Process of preparing the ozonide followed by decomposing.

q: When ethene is passed into cold dilute potassium permanganate solution, _____ glycol is formed.
e: When ethene is passed into cold dilute potassium permanganate solution, ethene glycol is formed. Listen for ethene in that sentence.

q: In the hydroxylation of alkenes, the colour of 1% dilute $KMnO_4$ solution is _____.
e: In the hydroxylation of alkenes, the colour of 1% dilute KMnO_4 solution is discharged. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.

q: The common name of ethene is _____.
e: The common name of ethene is ethylene. The common name of ethene is. Ethylene is the word this version is asking about.

q: In the IUPAC naming of alkenes, the number of the first carbon of the double bond is placed directly in front of the _____.
e: In the IUPAC naming of alkenes, the number of the first carbon of the double bond is placed directly in front of the root name. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.

q: Isomers that differ in the structures of the C-skeleton in the longer chain are called _____ isomers.
e: Isomers that differ in the structures of the C-skeleton in the longer chain are called chain isomers. Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ.

q: Dehydration of alcohols results in the loss of _____.
e: Dehydration of alcohols results in the loss of water. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. Dehydration of an alcohol removes H and OH from adjacent carbons to make an alkene and water.

q: In the dehydrohalogenation of ethyl chloride, the reagent used is an alcoholic solution of _____.
e: In the dehydrohalogenation of ethyl chloride, the reagent used is an alcoholic solution of potassium hydroxide. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon.

q: Alkenes are all _____ than water.
e: Alkenes are all lighter than water. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.

q: Alkenes are _____ in water.
e: Alkenes are insoluble in water. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.
